text:
olivia: FYI customer C-7812 opened an urgent ticket — intermittent 502/504s from our hosted inference endpoint /v1/generate. They see 'TLS handshake timeout' and 'upstream closed connection' starting ~09:17 PDT. Happening from multiple customer IPs and regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1). Ticket Z-7812. Pasting the customer's curl failure below.
devon: can you paste the raw curl -v and a sample request id? want to see the TLS error and SNI/host headers.
olivia: here is what the customer sent (sanitized):
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXXX' 
*   Trying 34.200.10.12:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (34.200.10.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS 1.3 handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:1409442E:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```
deploy-bot: cert-rotation edge-primary: START 2025-09-18T09:05:12Z  ID=rot-9087
deploy-bot: cert-rotation edge-primary: COMPLETE 2025-09-18T09:06:03Z  ID=rot-9087
maria: I pulled edge logs around the customer's request ids. We're seeing resolver hits returning an old CNAME for some clients, and the TLS server cert presented doesn't include the intermediate chain — that can cause some clients to error with 'unknown ca'. sample dig from an affected host:
```
$ dig api.redwood.example.com +short
redwood-edge-old.cdn-provider.net.
```
devon: hmm, rotation finished at 09:06 but logs show a mix of new and old CNAMEs for ~10-12 minutes. Looks like a partial DNS propagation + stale resolver cache on a subset of our edge nodes. If a client hits an edge node that still points to the old backend, that backend is serving the new cert chain incorrectly (missing intermediate) -> handshake fails or times out as client retries.
samir: can we repro internally? I'll try resolving via the affected resolver and curl with --resolve to force hitting the old and new IPs.
samir: repro steps I ran (internal):
```
# force old backend IP
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:52.16.11.9 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
# force new backend IP
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:34.200.10.12 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
samir: old IP -> TLS handshake timeout / alert unknown ca, new IP -> 200 OK. So we can reproduce by hitting the node that still had the old CNAME mapping.
devon: ran tcpdump on the edge node (old backend path) — TLS ClientHello then nothing, server RST after ~10s. snippet:
```
12:09:21.123456 IP 10.0.1.5.49234 > 52.16.11.9.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
12:09:21.234567 IP 52.16.11.9.443 > 10.0.1.5.49234: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
# then repeated client retries
```
maria: quick status check — rotation script updated certs but failed to include the intermediate chain on a subset of backend hosts (packaging bug). Combined with low DNS TTLs and aggressive resolver caching, some clients continued to get an old CNAME mapping that pointed at backends with partial chain -> intermittent handshake failures.
oncall_erin: mitigation plan in progress:
- rollback rotation on affected backend pool (edge-primary) to previous cert bundle (temporary)  -> applied
- force reissue with complete chain and re-deploy to pool (fix) -> in progress
- purge internal edge DNS cache and bump TTL for the domain to avoid mixed CNAMEs -> purged and bumped TTL to 60s
- monitor error rates and customer ticket
devon: I've pushed a hotfix to the rotation tool to ensure full-chain is packaged (includes intermediates). CI run green. Deploying to staging then canary to edge-primary now.
oncall_erin: rolled back and then re-deployed fixed certs to the affected nodes at 09:23 PDT. Purged resolver caches at 09:25. Added temporary routing rule so affected customer IPs preferentially go to nodes with validated certs while we finish rollout.
olivia: updated customer with mitigation notes and asked them to test. They sent a quick validation at 09:28 PDT: all requests returned 200 and no TLS errors in their environment. They confirmed reduced 502s to zero over a 6 minute window.
devon: follow-ups: 
- postmortem item: rotation tool must verify chain with `openssl verify -show_chain` before marking complete
- increase canary duration for cert rotations from 1 minute to 5 minutes
- add automated check to detect mixed-CNAME serving across edge nodes
maria: monitoring alert thresholds lowered temporarily to catch any regression. FWIW metrics: 502 spike peaked at 2.3% of requests for the tenant and is now back to baseline <0.1%.
olivia: closing the support escalation once customer confirms stability. Ticket Z-7812 will be updated with root cause (rotation packaging bug + DNS propagation), mitigation, and follow-ups. TY everyone :white_check_mark:
